mode: Tower browsing and inspection game interface in the accepted GitHub office
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / game interface concept.
Create a finished in-game TOWER BROWSER AND INSPECTION SCREEN based on the imagined GitHub office in image 1. The user has accepted this office direction and asks to use it to imagine how players browse and review Towers. One cohesive landscape 16:9 game screenshot-style mock-up, high resolution, sharp readable UI. This must be a usable GAME COLLECTION INTERFACE inside that very office, not an office-only picture and not a normal web dashboard.

REFERENCE PRIORITY:
Image 1 is the PRIMARY world and atmosphere reference. Preserve its warm oak worktables, ivory architecture, charcoal GitHub contribution wall, branching pendant lamps, glass Review room, lavender seating, leafy low-poly planters and broad campus windows.
Image 2 supplies APPROVED FUNCTIONAL CONTENT and basic left/center/right hierarchy ONLY. Do NOT copy its giant white monitor frame or replace the office with that earlier console. Bring those interactions to the oak desk in image 1.
Image 3 is the canonical orange Developer model. Preserve its design exactly.
Image 4 is the actual game's campus rendering and low-poly style reference.

COMPOSITION — A PLAYER AT THE TOWER WORKBENCH:
Move the camera in toward the shared oak worktable from image 1, looking gently down across it at a readable nearly frontal three-quarter angle. The player is browsing Towers at this table. Make the selected character visually dominant, floating physically above a small inspection plinth in the CENTER of the table.
The lower two-thirds of the image contain a comfortable, coherent interactive workbench: left portrait collection, center live 3D Tower, right visual stats, and one animation selection row along the near edge. The upper third and room margins retain unmistakable context from the GitHub office: the contribution-block wall and GitHub sign, branch pendant, glass Review room to the left, daylight/teal trees through the right windows. Avoid giant UI screens hiding the room.
Keep the office's real furniture proportions; the close camera provides model/label size, not giant room-sized monitors. No duplicate orange Developer on a second desk in the background. Repurpose or leave the previous rear alcove quiet.

UI FITS THE FURNITURE:
Use compact dark-charcoal panels with thin ivory or muted-indigo rims, restrained shadows and a visible slim lower lip. Panels appear docked or seated on the desk, with minimally tilted faces for legibility. Let the oak tabletop remain visibly continuous between them. The central live model is in open room space, never painted onto a flat screen.
The portrait collection may be a thin physical rack of selectable portrait plaques supported at the left desk edge. The stats may be a single slim angled instrument panel at the right desk edge. The animation choices are a small, tactile rail built into the near edge of the desk. No enormous shell enclosing the whole UI. No sci-fi cockpit armor, thick gaming monitor bezels, neon holographic walls or flat HTML rectangles pasted over the office.
Typography is crisp Mona Sans-style, with a clear title, quiet supporting text, sentence-case labels, and consistent Octicon-like small leading symbols. Color follows the previous Primer Brand direction: charcoal surfaces, off-white text, pale-indigo selected state, subtle teal accent. The warm oak and room's green acoustic tiles remain visible.

TOP GAME NAVIGATION:
A quiet compact HUD at upper left reads "Copilot Hub / Tower Codex". Keep the original small COPILOT identity where useful without overwhelming the office's existing GitHub sign.
A clearly readable tactile "Back to Hub" button at upper right with an arrow-left icon. No browser chrome, extra app navigation, sign-in buttons or toolbar clutter.

LEFT — BROWSE TOWERS:
Heading "Towers". Seven visible portrait choices, neatly arranged in a narrow two-column rack with the last card occupying one slot. Names exactly:
"Base", "Developer", "Tester", "Analyst", "Security", "Architect", "Linter".
Each has a clear character portrait and readable name. Base remains purple, Developer orange, Security blue and Linter yellow, matching image 2. For any not-yet-available model, use a quiet neutral head silhouette, not an invented new character. Do NOT use padlock icons or invent unlock levels.
Developer alone is selected with a pale-indigo rim and a small check marker. Cards have slight thickness and short contact shadows. They should feel like collectible Tower dossiers, not a business app list.
Do not add redundant filters/search for this small visible roster. Clicking a portrait is understood to swap the center model and stats in place.

CENTER — INSPECT THE TOWER:
Large clear title "Developer", subtitle "Direct-output specialist". Place these as a calm readable nameplate over/behind the model area without covering the character.
The canonical head occupies generous space, approximately a third of the screen height. Head only; faceted orange swept spikes, dark angular goggles with teal lenses, black face with exactly two cyan eye strokes, cream ear discs with curly-brace mark. No body, new accessories or redesigned silhouette.
The character hovers above a low faceted ivory/dark-blue plinth on the oak table with a restrained teal rim. Add a soft contact shadow below it. A faint unnumbered radius ring on the tabletop helps sell the live model.
Small orbit arrows around the model; a compact camera "Reset" key nearby. A crisp quiet hint reads "Drag to rotate · Tilt · Zoom". Camera controls must be distinct from animation controls.

RIGHT — VISUAL CAPABILITIES:
Heading "Stats". Five labeled visual rows with small consistent monochrome Octicon-style icons:
"Damage" with zap; "Work" with code; "Action speed" with meter; "Range" with crosshairs; "Compute" with cpu.
Use indigo segmented visual meters on dark tracks, with Compute separate and muted teal. Damage fills below halfway, Work full, Action speed full, Range around two-thirds, Compute mostly filled. Keep consistent scale and cell sizing within the display. Label plus fill length conveys the information.
ABSOLUTELY NO STAT NUMBERS, digits, units, fractions, percentages, prices, totals, upgrade costs, power scores or numeric labels anywhere.
Avoid gigantic pictograms or an overly dense stat table. Keep it calm and easy to compare when a different Tower is selected.

BOTTOM — ANIMATION SELECTION:
One row of exactly SEVEN selectable buttons, with these labels in this exact order:
"Rest", "Idle", "Work", "Move", "Place", "Hit", "Resolve".
Heading "Animations". Small leading icons may be moon, pulse, tools, arrow-both, package, zap, sparkle.
Idle alone is selected, with a pale-indigo face, dark label and small check. Others have neutral charcoal faces and light labels. Low-profile rounded-rectangle buttons retain physical depth, a small lower edge and contact shadows. There must be exactly seven buttons and no extra blank key.
Selecting a button is all the user needs to play that animation.
NO SPEED SELECTOR, play/pause button, timeline, scrubber, replay button, loop switch or numeric playback multipliers. "Action speed" above is only a Tower stat.

WORLD AND POLISH:
Keep the approved warm GitHub office recognizably present, rather than reverting to the old all-ivory console or generating a different room. A single mug, a closed notebook and one small planter can sit at the outer desk margins, but do not obstruct any control.
The style must remain the Hub's matte low-poly game world: simple faceted plants, broad daylight, modest bevels, gentle shadows, no photoreal fabric grain or wood grain, no bloom-heavy neon, no cinematic depth of field. UI lettering stays clean and readable across the whole composition, not dramatically perspective warped.
No extra characters, giant corporate slogans, tooltips obscuring things, artboard labels or comparison frames. This image is one cohesive, believable player-facing Tower collection screen, with the welcoming GitHub office as its real setting.
